results.title: 😸 Watch your language | Product Hunt
results.content:
•Hamdori ↗ — A tiny 3D hamster that lives on your desktop

Hamdori is a golden hamster modelled in 3D rather than drawn in pixels, living in a small window in the corner of the screen. Pet him with the cursor and his eyes close. He nibbles seeds while you type, stops when you stop, and if you walk off he burrows into his bedding until the mouse moves again. There is a 25-minute timer, after which he empties his cheeks. It asks for no Accessibility or Screen Recording permission, and the only thing it learns about your typing on a Mac is how many times a key went down, which is more thought about permissions than most apps with a hamster in them.

This Weekend's Top Products [...] •magpie ↗ — everything you’ve saved, in one visual library

magpie is one library for everything you have saved somewhere else. It pulls in your Instagram saves, Pinterest boards, X bookmarks and Are.na channels, then indexes them by what is actually in the picture, so a search for calm product shots with warm light brings back the images that look like that instead of the ones somebody captioned that way. Start a project, describe the brief, and it fills with the saves that fit. Anything pulled in stays pulled in, so a reference survives the original post being deleted.

@galdayanThanks for asking! On macOS I use CGEventSourceCounterForEventType(kCGEventSourceStateHIDSystemState, kCGEventKeyDown). It returns a count of key-down events, with no key codes, characters or app names. Hamdori checks it every 0.1 seconds, and when the count goes up, he nibbles.

The app never asks for Input Monitoring, and in my testing this call works without any permission prompt.

On Windows I use GetLastInputInfo, which only gives the time of the last input, not a key-press count.
